subject: FinLytics — performance SLOs (p95/p99) follow-up
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@finlytics.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: FinLytics / Redwood — perf SLOs follow-up

Hi Laura / Marissa,

Thanks again for the call today — really helpful to understand Redwood's serving model. Quick recap from our side and a few follow-ups so we can scope a short POC: 

What we discussed (short):
- End-to-end p95 / p99 latency targets for our customer-facing inference: currently aiming for p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 450ms for typical chat flows (we're measuring end-to-end from client SDK send->first-streamed token and final completion).
- Streaming is critical (we stream token-by-token to clients).
- Peak concurrency: ~50 concurrent user streams under normal peak; burst to ~120 for 5–10m windows.
- Typical request size: ~300–400 input tokens, avg response ~220 tokens.
- Current provider (ProviderX) observed: p95 ~320ms, p99 ~600ms (end-to-end), which is why we're evaluating options.

What we need from Redwood to qualify:
1) Confirmation that hosted API can meet p95/p99 targets at our concurrency + burst profile (or recommended configuration for Dedicated).
2) Clarify measurement methodology Redwood uses for p95/p99 (end-to-end vs server-side only, streaming first-byte vs completion).
3) Test plan: rough timeline and what artifacts you need (payloads, test API key, expected measurement windows).

I've attached a zip with a handful of ProviderX traces and a sample payload set (finlytics-provider-traces.zip). Happy to provide a short sandbox key for the PoC.

Next steps from our side: share sample payloads + grant a temporary test key if you want to schedule a perf run. Also let us know whether you need us to simulate long-tail bursts or whether Redwood prefers you run internal synthetic load.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Product Lead, FinLytics
samir@finlytics.com
+1 415-555-0178

Attachment: finlytics-provider-traces.zip (contains traces.csv, sample_payloads.json)
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FinLytics / Redwood — perf SLOs follow-up

Samir — thanks for the clear recap and the trace bundle. Really helpful. Re-summarizing and proposing concrete next steps so we can scope a short POC: 

Recap (Redwood understanding):
- Target: p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 450ms (end-to-end, includes client->Redwood->client roundtrip, streaming-first-token measurement unless otherwise requested).
- Streaming: token-by-token streaming required (we support chunked SSE / HTTP2 streaming).
- Concurrency profile: steady 50 concurrent streams, bursts up to ~120 for short windows.
- Example payload sizes: 300–400 tokens input, ~200–250 token output.

Questions / clarifications for you:
- Can you confirm avg tokens per request and peak sustained QPS during peak minute? (Samir's note said avg request size ~300–400 tokens; please confirm a QPS number).
- Do you have strict TLS/KMS requirements for the PoC?

Proposed POC plan (attach: redwood-perf-test-plan.xlsx):
1) Redwoods runs a baseline hosted API perf run using your sample payloads (you provide a sandbox API key / sample traffic).
2) We'll run two modes: streaming-first-byte latency and full-completion latency.
3) Load profile: ramp to 50 concurrent streams for 30m, then schedule 3x short burst windows to 120 concurrency for 10m each.
4) Acceptance criteria: p95 <= 250ms AND p99 <= 450ms for streaming-first-byte on the steady profile. If we miss, we'll iterate config (batching, concurrency sharding, quantization model variant).
5) Timeline: prep (you share payloads + key) 2 business days, perf run within 3 business days after that, initial report within 24 hours of run.

Owners: Laura (engage FinLytics, coordinate data & key), Marissa (oversee test and interpret results), Aditya (will run the load harness / k6 + internal runner).

Can you confirm the QPS and whether you want Redwood to simulate client SDK network conditions (we can add jitter and throttling to approximate mobile networks)?

If this sounds good I'll schedule a quick 30m sync with your engineering lead to confirm test harness details.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-perf-test-plan.xlsx
From: Samir Patel <samir@finlytics.com>

Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:10:00 -07:00

Thanks Laura — that plan looks good. Quick answers: 
- Avg tokens per request: 350 input / 220 output.
- Peak sustained QPS during peak minute: ~18–22 QPS (mostly chat fans out as streams).
- Concurrency: steady ~45–55, bursts up to 120.
- TLS/KMS: TLS mandatory; we use customer-managed keys in production but for the PoC a standard TLS connection is fine.
- Network conditions: we'd like Redwood to run with our typical mobile jitter profile for one of the runs (simulate 100–200ms variable latency + occasional packet loss).

I'm attaching the ProviderX traces we referenced (finlytics-provider-traces.zip) and I've added our HubSpot deal id in case you want to attach notes: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/3245. We can provide a short-lived API key — I'll coordinate offline with Laura.

Happy to sync on Wednesday morning if that helps (we're PST).

Best,
Samir

Subject: Re: FinLytics / Redwood — perf SLOs follow-up

Samir — great, thanks for the numbers. A few technical clarifications and the proposed acceptance criteria so we're all aligned before the run: 

Measurement methodology:
- For streaming-first-byte p95/p99 we measure from Redwood ingress (Redwood edge) receiving the request to the first token flushed to the client (this aligns closely with your client SDK timing; we can also run a true end-to-end measurement if you provide a test client endpoint).
- Full-completion latency measured from request start to final token delivered.

Acceptance criteria (steady-state):
- Streaming-first-byte: p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 450ms (measured at Redwood edge under your concurrency profile).
- Completion: p95 <= 600ms (informational for now).

Test schedule & ownership:
- Wed 2027-07-07: prep call (15m) — confirm API key + payloads.
- Thu 2027-07-08: baseline run (steady 50 concurrent streams, 30m).
- Fri 2027-07-09: burst profile + mobile jitter simulation.

Tech notes for the run:
- Aditya will use k6 with our streaming harness and will need a sandbox key + 2 sample payload files (small/large).
- Please include one representative long response (500+ tokens) so we exercise KV cache behavior.

Next steps (action items):
1) Samir: share sandbox API key + sample payloads (done: Provider traces attached; need sample payloads & key).
2) Laura: set up the 15m prep call and share calendar invite.
3) Aditya: prep k6 script and confirm infra for the runs.

I'll capture results in a short post-run recap and recommend config changes (batching, model selection, quantization) if we see regressions. Looking forward — excited to see how we perform vs ProviderX.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
